title: "Frontier developers write maybe 1-2% of code. The rest is agents." — Clare Liguori, AWS
talk_summary: Clare Liguori reports Amazon pilots where teams got step-function gains only when they changed working habits: invest in agent context, feed agents with self-validation instead of babysitting, make intent explicit, and shift testing left. She also warns that adoption requires slowing down first and creates new bottlenecks in decision-making and review.

takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent makes a mistake, they ask what missing skill or steering instruction caused it, then add that context; they also prune stale rules as models improve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what am I missing in my skills files? What am I missing in my steering files

takeaways.technique: Feed agents with self-validation, don't babysit
takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents the task plus validation criteria so they can self-correct and only return when they meet a quality bar, enabling parallel unattended runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: feeding it what it needs to do and how it can self-validate
takeaways.numbers: median 4.5x productivity; some >10x; pathfinder up to 20x

takeaways.technique: Local deterministic mocks for fast feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: They invest in mock services that run locally with deterministic responses so agents can test and self-correct without spinning up live dependencies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: mock services that run entirely locally with deterministic responses because it lets the agent do everything locally

takeaways.technique: Explicit intent via spec before code
takeaways.what_they_do: For ambiguous features, they write or generate a specification and iterate on the document before letting agents change code across the codebase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a lot easier to to iterate with the model in kind of a back and forth conversation about a document than it is about code
takeaways.numbers: Prime Video 10-day sprint cut estimate from 90 weeks to 24; senior engineer spent 3 weeks creating small well-scoped tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: They improve existing tool error messages so the model understands what failed and can recover instead of guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: improve existing tools error messages so that the model knew what was going on when it failed

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat decision-making and launch review as the new bottleneck and push fast decisions, especially reversible ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more that you can make fast decisions, especially ones that are easy to be reversed, the better
takeaways.numbers: code only takes 1-2 months to write; decision/launch review become long pole
